status: PASS independent source and mathematical review before bounded controls
claims: No globally minimum circuit has a gate equal to an earlier wire on all edge/MIS samples: alias deletion preserves those samples, hence exact monotone output.
No globally minimum circuit has a gate dominated by an earlier wire that is at least as true on positive edges and at most as true on maximal false rows: aliasing improves both sample classes.
The previous-target flag guards both operand incomparability and optional uniqueness/domination; the first exact target itself still satisfies all cuts.

A normalized minimum prefix pads by repeating its last operation on the previous output and one original operand. OR padding introduces no owner; AND padding has a true earlier AND ancestor on every edge.
First-gate symmetry stays fixed; padding directly reads its predecessor, so adjacent-independent ordering does not forbid it.
Decoder replays the earliest target on all assignments and reports its profile separately from the whole circuit.
scope: Mathematical finite-model completeness for normalized global-minimum prefixes; not a Lean normalization theorem, a proved lower bound, or a held-gap result. Aliasing is not claimed to preserve profile for arbitrary nonminimum circuits.
